questions.question: On 8–9 November 2025, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the National Judicial Academy hosted a national conference in Bhopal focusing on which area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Criminal Laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **8–9 November**, the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** and the **National Judicial Academy (NJA)** organized a national conference in **Bhopal**, **Madhya Pradesh**, dedicated to the implementation and nuances of the **New Criminal Laws**.
 
• The conference served as a critical platform for members of the **judiciary**, **legal experts**, and **administrative officials** to discuss the transition from colonial-era statutes to a more modern, **citizen-centric** legal framework.
 
• The primary focus was on the three transformative acts: the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**.
 
• Discussions highlighted the shift from a "punishment-based" system to a "justice-based" system, emphasizing the **decolonization** of the Indian **criminal justice system**.
 
• The event underscored the importance of **technological integration**, such as the mandatory **videography** of crime scenes and the use of **digital evidence**, which are core components of the new legal reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**:
 
 
• It replaces the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** of **1860**.
 
• It introduces **community service** as a form of punishment for specific petty offenses and defines **terrorism** and **organized crime** for the first time within a general criminal code.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**:
 
 
• It replaces the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC)** of **1973**.
 
• It mandates **strict timelines** for **investigations**, **trials**, and the delivery of **judgments**, aiming to reduce the massive backlog of cases in Indian courts.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023**:
 
 
• It replaces the **Indian Evidence Act** of **1872**.
 
• It expands the definition of **documentary evidence** to include **electronic or digital records**, giving them the same legal standing as paper documents.
 
 
 
• The implementation of these laws officially began on **July 1, 2024**, marking a significant milestone in India's **legislative history**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Judicial Academy (NJA)**: Located in **Bhopal**, it is a premier institute for the **training** and **capacity building** of judges across India. Its role in this conference was to ensure the **judiciary** is well-equipped to interpret the **new statutes** correctly.
 
• **Decolonization Objective**: A major theme of the conference was removing the **colonial mindset** embedded in the old laws (which were drafted by the **British**) and replacing them with laws that reflect **contemporary Indian values**.
 
• **Victim Rights**: The new laws grant more rights to **victims**, including the right to be **informed** about the progress of an investigation within **90 days**.
 
• **Zero FIR**: The **BNSS** formally institutionalizes the concept of **Zero FIR**, allowing any person to file a **First Information Report** at any police station, regardless of the **jurisdiction** where the crime occurred.

questions.question: Researchers from which institutions discovered a new prion called SNG2 in January 2025?

options.text: Delhi University and Council of Scientific & Industrial Research - Delhi
Amity University - Mohali and Institute of Microbial Technology - Chandigarh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amity University - Mohali and Institute of Microbial Technology - Chandigarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, a team of researchers from **Amity University, Mohali** and the **Council of Scientific & Industrial Research - Institute of Microbial Technology (CSIR-IMTECH), Chandigarh**, announced the discovery of a novel prion.
 
• The newly identified prion has been named **SNG2**, an acronym for **Supersaturating Non-Amyloidogenic Globular 2**.
 
• This discovery is a landmark in the field of **molecular biology** as it identifies a prion that behaves differently from traditional disease-causing proteins.
 
• The **SNG2** prion was discovered in the yeast species **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**, which is a common model organism used for studying cellular processes.
 
• Unlike pathological prions that form toxic **amyloid fibrils**, **SNG2** forms **globular structures** that are **non-amyloidogenic**, meaning they do not aggregate into the stiff fibers typical of neurodegenerative diseases.
 
• The researchers found that **SNG2** acts as a functional switch, helping the organism survive and adapt under **environmental stress**, such as nutrient deprivation or temperature changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prions and Proteostasis:** 
 
 
• Prions are **misfolded proteins** that can induce normal versions of the same protein to also misfold. This chain reaction usually leads to **protein aggregation**.
 
• In humans, prions are notorious for causing fatal conditions like **Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD)** and **Kuru**, as well as **Mad Cow Disease** in cattle.
 
 
 
• **Functional Prions:**
 
 
• While many prions are harmful, "functional prions" are those that provide a biological benefit. **SNG2** is a prime example of a **functional prion** that assists in **cellular memory** and stress response.
 
• This discovery suggests that protein-based **epigenetic inheritance** is more diverse and common than previously understood.
 
 
 
• **The Role of SNG2:**
 
 
• The **SNG2** protein remains in a **supersaturated state** within the cell until triggered by stress.
 
• Its **non-amyloidogenic** nature is crucial because it allows the cell to utilize the protein's aggregated form without suffering the **cellular toxicity** that usually leads to cell death in amyloid-related diseases.
 
 
 
• **Institutions Involved:**
 
 
• **Amity University, Mohali** is a leading private research university in **Punjab**, known for its focus on **biotechnology**.
 
• **CSIR-IMTECH**, located in **Chandigarh**, is a premier national laboratory under the **Ministry of Science and Technology**, specializing in **microbial engineering** and protein science.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The discovery of **SNG2** in **2025** provides new insights into how proteins can store information and help organisms adapt to their surroundings without changing their **DNA**.
 
• The study utilized advanced **biophysical techniques** and **fluorescence microscopy** to observe the transition of the protein into its **globular prion state**.
 
• Understanding the mechanism of **non-amyloidogenic** prions like **SNG2** could eventually lead to new therapeutic strategies for human diseases like **Alzheimer’s** and **Parkinson’s**, by teaching scientists how to prevent proteins from forming toxic **amyloid** clumps.
 
• This research underscores the importance of **inter-institutional collaboration** in **India** for achieving breakthroughs in fundamental **biological sciences**.

questions.question: Which Indian official chaired the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL) meetings, recommending the revision of blanket 10-km ESZ guidelines in mid-2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minister of Environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL)** is a high-level statutory body chaired by the **Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**. While the full **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**, the **Standing Committee** handles the routine and technical approvals for projects.
 
• In recent deliberations aimed for completion by **mid-2025**, the **Minister of Environment** has overseen the recommendation to revise the traditional **blanket 10-km Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ)** guidelines.
 
• The **10-km** radius guideline was originally part of the **Wildlife Conservation Strategy** adopted in **2002**, which suggested that lands within **10 kilometres** of the boundaries of **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries** should be notified as eco-fragile zones.
 
• The proposed revision led by the **Minister of Environment** aims to make these zones more site-specific rather than adhering to a uniform distance, acknowledging that geographical and biological requirements vary across different **Protected Areas** in **India**.
 
• The **SC-NBWL** plays a critical role under the **Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972**, as it is the body that examines the impact of developmental activities on wildlife habitats before granting clearances. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Minister of Environment.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ)**:
 
 
• These zones are notified by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
 
• The primary **function** of an **ESZ** is to act as a "shock absorber" for **Protected Areas** by regulating activities around them to minimize negative impacts on the ecosystem.
 
• Activities in these zones are classified into three categories: **Prohibited** (e.g., commercial mining, sawmills), **Regulated** (e.g., felling of trees, hotels/resorts), and **Permitted** (e.g., ongoing agricultural practices, rainwater harvesting).
 
 
 
• **Legal Precedents**:
 
 
• In **June 2022**, the **Supreme Court** of **India** directed that every **National Park** and **Wildlife Sanctuary** in the **country** must have a mandatory **ESZ** of at least **1 kilometre**.
 
• However, in **April 2023**, the **Supreme Court** modified this **judgement**, clarifying that the **1-km** rule would not be applicable where a specific **ESZ** notification had already been issued or where the **Protected Area** was located along interstate boundaries.
 
 
 
• **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)**:
 
 
• It is a statutory organization constituted under **Section 5A** of the **Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• It serves as an apex body to review all wildlife-related matters and approve projects in and around **National Parks** and **Wildlife Sanctuaries**.
 
• The **NBWL** consists of **47 members**, including the **Prime Minister** as **Chairperson** and the **Minister of Environment** as the **Vice-Chairperson**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Standing Committee**: The **SC-NBWL** consists of the **Minister of Environment**, the **Member Secretary**, and other members nominated by the **Vice-Chairperson**. It exercises the powers delegated to it by the full board, making it the most active regulatory body for wildlife clearances in **India**.
 
• **Revision Rationale**: The move to revise the **10-km** blanket guideline is intended to address the **administrative** and **socio-economic** challenges faced by local communities living near **Protected Areas** while ensuring that conservation is not compromised.
 
• **Timeline**: The target date of **mid-2025** reflects the government's **policy cycle** to streamline environmental clearances and update aging conservation frameworks to align with modern **data** and **ecological mapping**.
 
• **Jurisdiction**: No alteration of the boundaries of a **National Park** or a **Wildlife Sanctuary** can be made except on a recommendation of the **National Board for Wildlife**, highlighting the **legal authority** of the committee chaired by the **Minister of Environment**.
</ul

questions.question: What maximum sustained wind speed range was forecast for Cyclone Montha before landfall in October 2025?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**90-100 km/h**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclone Montha** was a tropical cyclone that developed in the **North Indian Ocean** basin, specifically in the **Bay of Bengal**, during **October 2025**.
 
• The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** issued bulletins forecasting that the system would maintain a **maximum sustained wind speed** in the range of **90-100 km/h** just before making landfall.
 
• With wind speeds reaching **90-100 km/h**, the system was classified as a **Severe Cyclonic Storm**. This category typically involves wind speeds between **89 km/h and 117 km/h**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the 90-100 km/h range is correct.***
 
• The forecast also indicated **gusting** speeds reaching up to **110 km/h**, which posed a significant threat to temporary structures and agricultural crops in the **coastal districts**.
 
• The landfall was projected to impact the **eastern coast of India**, specifically affecting the states of **Odisha** and **West Bengal**, leading to the mobilization of **NDRF (National Disaster Response Force)** teams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Cyclones:**
 
 
• The **IMD** classifies cyclonic disturbances based on their **maximum sustained surface wind speed (MSW)**. A **Cyclonic Storm** has speeds of **62-88 km/h**, while a **Severe Cyclonic Storm** ranges from **89-117 km/h**.
 
• If the winds exceed **118-165 km/h**, it is termed a **Very Severe Cyclonic Storm**, and anything above **221 km/h** is a **Super Cyclonic Storm**.
 
 
 
• **Sustained Wind Speed:**
 
 
• In the context of Indian meteorology, **sustained wind speed** is usually measured as a **3-minute average** or a **10-minute average** at a height of **10 meters**.
 
• This metric is crucial for determining the **potential damage** to infrastructure and the height of the **storm surge** expected during landfall.
 
 
 
• **Cyclone Naming:**
 
 
• The name **Montha** was contributed by **Myanmar** as part of the naming protocol established by the **WMO/ESCAP** Panel on Tropical Cyclones.
 
• Naming helps in **disaster risk communication** and avoids confusion when multiple systems are active simultaneously in the same **geographical region**.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Mitigation:**
 
 
• A wind range of **90-100 km/h** is strong enough to cause the **uprooting of trees**, damage to **power lines**, and significant **storm surges** of about **0.5 to 1.0 meter** above the astronomical tide.
 
• The **Integrated Cyclone Adventure System** and **satellite imagery** (such as **INSAT-3DR**) are used to track the **latitude** and **longitude** of the eye of the storm.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** **October** and **November** are considered the peak **post-monsoon cyclone season** for the **Bay of Bengal** due to high **sea surface temperatures**.
 
• **Landfall Characteristics:** The **landfall** process involves the center of the **cyclone eye** moving over the coast, where the highest **wind pressure** is often felt in the **right forward quadrant** of the storm.
 
• **Warning Protocols:** The **IMD** uses a **four-stage warning system**: **Pre-Cyclone Watch**, **Cyclone Alert** (Yellow), **Cyclone Warning** (Orange), and **Post-Landfall Outlook** (Red).
</ul

questions.question: According to the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, what was the forest cover in India as a percentage of its total geographical area in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21.76%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025** was released by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, Government of India.
 
• According to the report, the **forest cover** in India as a percentage of its **total geographical area** for the year **2023** was recorded as **21.76%**.
 
• This indicator is part of the monitoring mechanism for **SDG Goal 15**, which focuses on **"Life on Land"** and aims to protect, restore, and promote the sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems.
 
• The data utilized in the **NIF Progress Report** is primarily derived from the assessments conducted by the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)** and is mapped to the progress of the **United Nations' 2030 Agenda**.
 
• Maintaining and increasing the **forest cover** is essential for **biodiversity conservation**, carbon sequestration, and ensuring ecological balance in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India State of Forest Report (ISFR)**:
 
 
• The **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**, an organization under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**, publishes this **biennial report**.
 
• The **ISFR 2021** assessment (the **17th cycle**) reported the total forest cover of India to be **7,13,789 sq km**.
 
• This figure represented **21.71%** of the **total geographical area** of India (**3,287,469 sq km**). The **21.76%** figure in the **2025 Progress Report** reflects the updated indicators within the **National Indicator Framework**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Forest Cover**:
 
 
• Forest cover is classified into three categories based on canopy density: **Very Dense Forest** (density > 70%), **Moderately Dense Forest** (density 40%–70%), and **Open Forest** (density 10%–40%).
 
• Any land with a **tree canopy density** of more than **10%** and an area of more than **1 hectare** is considered forest cover, regardless of land ownership or legal status.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Data**:
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has the largest **forest cover** in terms of **area** in the country.
 
• In terms of **percentage** of geographical area, **Mizoram** ranks highest at approximately **84.53%**, followed by **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 15 (SDG 15)**:
 
 
• This goal targets the **sustainable management of forests**, combating **desertification**, and halting **land degradation** and **biodiversity loss**.
 
• India's **National Indicator Framework** tracks **12 indicators** specifically under SDG 15 to monitor domestic progress.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Forest Policy, 1988**: The government aims to bring **33%** of the total geographical area under **forest and tree cover** to ensure environmental stability and ecological security.
 
• **Tree Cover**: Unlike forest cover, **tree cover** refers to isolated or small patches of trees (less than **1 hectare**) found outside the recorded forest area. When combined, the **Total Forest and Tree Cover** in India is approximately **24.62%** of the total area.
 
• **Carbon Stock**: The total **carbon stock** in the country's forests is estimated to be around **7,204 million tonnes**, showing an increase compared to previous assessments, which is a key metric for **climate change mitigation**.
 
• **NIF Progress Report 2025**: This report serves as a critical document for **policymakers** to understand the gap between current achievements and the **2030 targets** set by the **United Nations**.
</ul

questions.question: Which body emphasised safety audits for women in public spaces during a symposium in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Human Rights Commission**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• In **June 2025**, the **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** convened a significant national symposium specifically addressing the **safety and security of women** in public and semi-public spaces across India. 
 
• The commission strongly advocated for the institutionalization of **safety audits**, which are systematic evaluations of the physical and social environment of **urban spaces** to identify factors that contribute to a lack of safety for **women**. 
 
• The **NHRC** highlighted that these audits should focus on **infrastructure gaps** such as poor **street lighting**, lack of **CCTV coverage**, and inadequate **public transport** facilities that hinder women's mobility. ***Hence, the correct answer is the National Human Rights Commission.*** 
 
• The body emphasized that **urban local bodies (ULBs)** and **police departments** must collaborate with **civil society organizations** to conduct these audits periodically to ensure **gender-responsive urban planning**. 
 
• During the symposium, the **NHRC** also pointed out the necessity of **technological integration**, such as mobile-based **panic buttons** and real-time **tracking systems**, as a follow-up to the findings of the **safety audits**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):** 
 
 
• It is a **Statutory public body** established on **12 October 1993** under the **Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993**. 
 
• The commission is headquartered in **New Delhi** and serves as the watchdog of human rights in the country, relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity of the individual as guaranteed by the **Constitution of India**. 
 
• The **Chairperson** and members are appointed by the **President of India** on the recommendations of a high-powered committee headed by the **Prime Minister**. 
 
 
 
• **Safety Audits and Urban Design:** 
 
 
• A **safety audit** is a participatory tool developed originally in **Canada** in the **1980s** to involve women in the assessment of their own safety in the **urban environment**. 
 
• In India, various **NGOs** like **Jagori** and **Safetipin** have pioneered the use of safety audits to map **safety scores** for different areas in cities like **Delhi**, **Mumbai**, and **Bengaluru**. 
 
• Key parameters of these audits include **lighting**, **openness**, **visibility**, **crowd**, **security**, and **walkpath** availability. 
 
 
 
• **Safe City Project:** 
 
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** has implemented the **Safe City Project** under the **Nirbhaya Fund** in **8 major cities**: **Ahmedabad**, **Bengaluru**, **Chennai**, **Delhi**, **Hyderabad**, **Kolkata**, **Lucknow**, and **Mumbai**. 
 
• This project aligns with the **NHRC's** recommendations by focusing on **smart policing**, **emergency response systems**, and **gender-sensitization** of the police force. 
 
• It also aims at improving **forensic facilities** and establishing **One Stop Centres (OSC)** for women in distress. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Article 21** of the **Indian Constitution** guarantees the **Right to Life and Personal Liberty**, which the **NHRC** interprets to include the right to move freely and safely in public spaces without fear of **gender-based violence**. 
 
• The **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11** specifically targets making cities and human settlements **inclusive**, **safe**, **resilient**, and **sustainable**, with a focus on providing universal access to safe, inclusive, and accessible **green and public spaces**, especially for women. 
 
• **Section 12** of the **PHRA, 1993**, empowers the **NHRC** to review the factors that inhibit the enjoyment of human rights and recommend appropriate **remedial measures** to the government. 
</ul

questions.question: Published in May 2025, Pavan K Varma’s Echoes of Eternity explores themes from which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian thought from Rigveda onward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Echoes of Eternity** is a significant literary work authored by **Pavan K Varma**, a renowned diplomat and writer, published in **May 2025**.
 
• The book serves as an extensive exploration of **Indian thought**, beginning with the **Rigveda**, which is considered the oldest of the four **Vedas** and a foundational text of **Indian philosophy**.
 
• The narrative traces the evolution of philosophical concepts over thousands of years, examining how ancient wisdom remains relevant in the **21st century**.
 
• The work focuses on the spiritual and metaphysical foundations of India, touching upon themes such as **Sanatana Dharma**, the nature of **consciousness**, and the continuity of the **Indian civilization**.
 
• Through this book, **Pavan K Varma** aims to make complex intellectual traditions accessible to a modern audience, bridging the gap between **ancient texts** and contemporary **societal values**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Author Profile:** **Pavan K Varma** is a former officer of the **Indian Foreign Service (IFS)** and has served as the **Ambassador of India** to several countries, including **Bhutan** and **Cyprus**. He has also been a member of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• **Literary Contributions:** He is well-known for his insightful books on **Indian culture** and **history**, such as **The Great Hindu Civilisation**, **Being Indian**, and **The Great Indian Middle Class**.
 
• **Significance of the Rigveda:** The **Rigveda** consists of **1,028 hymns** organized into **10 Mandalas**. It represents the earliest recorded form of **Indo-Aryan thought** and contains the **Gayatri Mantra**, which is central to **Hindu** tradition.
 
• **Context of the Book:** **Echoes of Eternity** emphasizes that **Indian thought** is not a static relic of the past but a living, breathing **intellectual heritage** that continues to influence global **spirituality** and **ethics**.
 
• **Theme of Continuity:** The book highlights the resilient nature of **Indian philosophical inquiry**, which has survived centuries of foreign invasions and **colonial rule** to remain a vital part of the nation's **identity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The book is released at a time when there is a growing global interest in **Indic knowledge systems** and **Vedic philosophy**.
 
• **Pavan K Varma** frequently utilizes his **diplomatic background** to provide a comparative perspective on how **Indian thought** differs from and complements **Western philosophical** traditions.
 
• The publication of **Echoes of Eternity** in **2025** marks another milestone in the author's career as a public **intellectual** and **cultural commentator**.
 
• Major themes in the book also include the concept of **Dharma**, the cycle of **Samsara**, and the pursuit of **Moksha**, which are core to the **Upanishadic** and **Vedic** eras.
</ul

questions.question: Which athlete set a pole vault world record with a clearance of 6.28 m in Wanda Diamond League meeting in Stockholm (June 2025)?

__
 
• The Swedish pole vaulter **Armand "Mondo" Duplantis** set a new world record by clearing a height of **6.28 m**.
 
• This record-breaking performance occurred during the **Wanda Diamond League** meeting held in **Stockholm**, **Sweden**, in **June 2025**.
 
• By clearing **6.28 m**, Duplantis once again improved upon his own previous global mark, cementing his status as the greatest pole vaulter in history.
 
• The event, known as the **Bauhaus-Galan**, saw **Duplantis** compete in front of a home crowd at the historic **Stockholm Olympic Stadium**.
 
• The **6.28 m** clearance was achieved on his **first attempt** (or as specified in the meet details), demonstrating his unmatched consistency at extreme heights. ***Hence, the correct answer is Armand Duplantis.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Armand Duplantis:**
 
 
• Born on **November 10, 1999**, in **Lafayette, Louisiana, USA**, he holds dual citizenship but represents **Sweden** in international competitions.
 
• He won the **Gold Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and the **Paris 2024 Olympics**, establishing a legacy of dominance.
 
• He was awarded the **World Athlete of the Year** title multiple times by **World Athletics**.
 
 
 
• **Renaud Lavillenie:**
 
 
• A **French** pole vaulter who held the world record of **6.16 m** from **2014 to 2020**.
 
• He won the **Olympic Gold** at the **2012 London Games** and remains one of the most decorated athletes in the sport's history.
 
 
 
• **Sam Kendricks:**
 
 
• An **American** pole vaulter and a **two-time World Champion** (**2017 and 2019**).
 
• He is known for his consistent podium finishes and for winning the **Bronze Medal** at the **2016 Rio Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Thiago Braz:**
 
 
• A **Brazilian** athlete who rose to fame by winning the **Olympic Gold Medal** at the **2016 Rio Olympics** with a then-Olympic record of **6.03 m**.
 
• He also secured a **Bronze Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wanda Diamond League:** This is an annual series of elite track and field athletic competitions, comprising **15** of the best invitational athletics meetings in the world. It was established in **2010** to replace the **IAAF Golden League**.
 
• **World Athletics:** The international governing body for the sport of athletics, which officially ratifies world records such as the **6.28 m** mark set by **Duplantis**.
 
• **Pole Vault Dynamics:** The sport involves using a flexible pole made of **carbon fiber** or **fiberglass**. World records can be set both **indoors** and **outdoors**, and since **2000**, World Athletics rules do not distinguish between the two for the overall world record.
</ul
